narrative_before: An employee interacted with a phishing email on a personal computer, which was infected with malware; when the employee connected to the bank's network over VPN, the attackers captured their login credentials (SANS). Using those valid credentials, the attackers exploited the absence of two-factor authentication on a web-development server and moved from it to more than 100 other servers across the network, including banking data-center systems and other lines of business. They collected customer data for ~83 million households and businesses and slowly exfiltrated gigabytes over months through multi-hop proxies, deleting log files to evade detection. Security personnel discovered the breach when a routine scan flagged a vulnerability on a charity-race website.

detection_moments.description: Initial access: VPN credentials captured from the infected personal PC and used to reach the 2FA-less web-development server.
detection_moments.evidence: 'employee used infected personal computer to connect to the victim system through a VPN ... used valid credentials to exploit the lack of 2-factor authentication into a web-development server' - CTID flow / SANS

detection_moments.description: Lateral movement from the web-development server to 100+ servers across banking lines of business.
detection_moments.evidence: 'moved from the web-development server to more than 100 other servers within the network' - CTID flow / SANS

attack_path: stolen VPN credentials used against web-dev server lacking 2FA - T1078 / T1190
lateral movement to 100+ internal servers (some via zero-days/custom malware) - T1078
ambiguities: 100+ servers are not individually named; modelled as a 3-host generic group (rule cap).
Flow lists zero-day and custom-malware edges for some lateral hops; not sub-typed per target host.
Detection: breach found via routine web vulnerability scan, not a specific host-compromise alert; m2 marks the lateral stage.
